websites.title: Websites
websites.unsupported: Website management needs a Debian or Ubuntu server with systemd, so it is not available on this machine.
websites.empty: No websites yet. Add your first one.
websites.domain_hint: Without http:// or www. First point the domain's A record to this server's IP address.
websites.created: {domain} is ready. Upload your files to {path}.
websites.ssl_note: Certificates come free from Let's Encrypt and renew automatically. By turning on HTTPS you accept the Let's Encrypt Subscriber Agreement.
websites.delete_body: This deletes the website's files, its Linux user and its certificate. It cannot be undone.
websites.wp_needs_db: WordPress needs MariaDB. Install it first on the page:
websites.wp_ssl_hint: Tip: turn on HTTPS first, so WordPress starts with an https:// address. If you turn it on later, the panel switches WordPress over for you.
websites.wp_user_hint: Avoid "admin": it is the first name attackers try.
websites.wp_password_hint: Leave empty to generate a strong password, or type 12 to 128 characters.
websites.wp_credentials_body: Save these details now: the password is not shown again. The installation runs below.
websites.delete_dbs: Also delete the databases linked to this website
websites.aliases_hint: One per line, such as www.example.com, or *.example.com for every subdomain (needs DNS validation). Each name must point to this server.
websites.reissue_needed: The domain names changed. Get a new certificate so HTTPS covers all of them.
websites.app_hint: Run in the website's app folder as its own user, with PORT set. Leave empty if the app is started otherwise (for example in Docker).
websites.php_pm_dynamic: Keep some ready (faster for busy sites)
websites.php_workers_hint: How many requests this site's PHP handles at the same time. Each worker can use up to the memory limit, so workers × memory should fit in the server's RAM.
websites.php_allow: Allow functions that are disabled for safety
websites.php_allow_hint: They let a hacked site run programs on the server. Allow one only if an application really needs it.
websites.app_runtime_hint: The app's service and "Install dependencies" use this runtime. Python apps get their own virtual environment in app/.venv.

databases.title: Databases
databases.unsupported: Database management needs a Debian or Ubuntu server, so it is not available on this machine.
databases.install_body: The panel will install the MariaDB database server from your distribution's packages, limit its memory use to suit this server and make it listen on this server only. This takes one to two minutes.
databases.name_hint: A user with the same name is created and may only use this database.
databases.password_hint: Leave empty to generate a strong password.
databases.change_password_body: Applications that use the old password stop working until you update them. WordPress sites created by the panel are updated automatically.
databases.delete_body: This deletes the database, all of its tables and its user. It cannot be undone.
databases.import_reset: Empty the database first (delete all of its tables)
databases.subtitle: MariaDB databases, each with its own user.
databases.remote_intro: Let programs on other machines connect to this database. Only the addresses you list can connect, and only to this database.
databases.remote_no_firewall: The ufw firewall is not installed. Remote access needs it to keep other addresses out.
databases.remote_firewall_inactive: The firewall is turned off, so port 3306 is open to everyone (MariaDB still only accepts the listed addresses). Turn it on:
databases.remote_restart_pending: MariaDB has to restart before it accepts remote connections.
databases.remote_restarting: MariaDB is restarting to listen on all interfaces: see the progress on the page.
databases.remote_hosts_hint: IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, or IPv4 ranges such as 10.1.0.0/16 (no wider than /16). At most {max}.
databases.remote_tip_firewall: The panel opens port {port} in the firewall for these addresses only, and creates the database user for each of them with the same password.
databases.remote_tip_static: Only list addresses you control and that do not change. Anyone who gets one of them, and the password, can reach the database.
databases.remote_tip_tls: Connections are not encrypted unless the client asks for TLS. Prefer an SSH tunnel or a VPN for sensitive data.
databases.remote_tip_restart: The first time remote access is turned on, and when it is turned off for the last database, MariaDB restarts. Websites lose their database for a few seconds.
databases.remote_connect_hint: Connect with the user {user} and the database password to this server's public IP address, port {port}.
databases.remote_off_confirm: Turn off remote access to {name}? Programs on other machines lose their connection.
databases.slow_intro: MariaDB can log every query that takes longer than a threshold. This helps to find what slows a website down. Logging adds a little work for the server, so turn it off when you are done.
databases.slow_not_running: MariaDB is not running. Start it on the Services page to change these settings.
databases.slow_count: {n} newest entry (at most {max}) | {n} newest entries (at most {max})
databases.slow_clear_confirm: Delete every entry of the slow query log?
databases.slow_cleared: The slow query log is empty.
databases.slow_empty: The log is empty. Turn logging on to collect slow queries.
databases.slow_enabled: Queries slower than {s} s are logged now, also after a restart.
databases.slow_disabled: Slow queries are no longer logged.

files.title: Files
files.overwrite_confirm: These files already exist and will be replaced: {names}. Continue?
files.action_chmod: Permissions for {name} (for example 0644 for files, 0755 for folders)
files.truncated: Only the first 5,000 items are shown.
files.discard_changes: You have unsaved changes. Close the editor anyway?
files.editor_hint: Ctrl+S saves. Files of up to 2 MB can be edited.
files.subtitle: Browse and edit files. Inside a website's folder, changes are confined to that website.
files.fetch_title: Download a file from a URL
files.fetch_hint: The file is saved in {dir} and belongs to the folder's owner. Only http and https, up to 2 GB; an existing file is never replaced.
files.search_hint: Upper and lower case are treated the same. Text search skips binary files and files over 2 MB. Symbolic links are not followed.
files.search_walked: {walked} item looked at | {walked} items looked at
files.search_truncated: The search stopped at a limit (20,000 items looked at, 200 results or 20 seconds). Search a smaller folder or use more precise words to see everything.
files.search_skipped: {n} file not read: binary or over 2 MB | {n} files not read: binary or over 2 MB
files.trash_hint: Items deleted in {scope} wait here for {days} day, then they are removed for good. Only root can read them. | Items deleted in {scope} wait here for {days} days, then they are removed for good. Only root can read them.
files.trash_summary: {n} item, {size} in total | {n} items, {size} in total
files.trash_empty_confirm: Delete the {n} item in this trash permanently? | Delete the {n} items in this trash permanently?
files.trash_occupied: Something else is at this path now: move it away to restore this item.
files.trash_truncated: Only the 1,000 most recently deleted items are shown.
files.delete_to_trash: They go to the trash, where they can be restored for 30 days.
files.delete_permanent_warn: Permanently deleted items, including folders with all their content, cannot be recovered. Use this for very large files, which would otherwise keep taking disk space in the trash.
files.moved_to_trash: {n} item moved to the trash. | {n} items moved to the trash.
files.deleted_permanently: {n} item deleted permanently. | {n} items deleted permanently.

backups.title: Backups
backups.now_hint: A website backup contains all of its files and the databases linked to it. Backups are kept on this server in /var/backups/panel.
backups.restore_site_body: The website's current files and the content of its databases are replaced by the backup. Changes made since the backup are lost.
backups.restore_db_body: The current content of the database is replaced by the backup. Changes made since the backup are lost.
backups.delete_confirm: Delete the backup {name} from this server and from remote storage?
backups.schedule_delete_confirm: Stop the automatic backups of {target}? Existing backups are kept.
backups.no_schedules: No automatic backups yet. Add a schedule so you never lose your work.
backups.storage_none: Not set up. Copies on another provider protect you if this server is lost.
backups.storage_hint: Any S3-compatible service works: Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2 (region auto), Backblaze B2, Wasabi or MinIO. Use an access key that may only use this bucket. The panel tests the settings before saving them.
backups.secret_keep: Leave empty to keep the current secret key.
backups.storage_saved: Remote storage works and was saved.
backups.storage_remove_confirm: Remove the remote storage settings? Backups already uploaded stay in the bucket.
backups.subtitle: Back up websites, databases and folders, on this server, in the cloud or on another server over SFTP.
backups.restore_app_body: The app's folder and data are replaced by the backup, and its containers restart. Changes made since the backup are lost.
backups.restore_app_passwords: Restoring also brings back the passwords saved in the backup: afterwards the app's credentials show those.
backups.folder_hint: Any folder of the server, such as /etc/nginx or /opt/app. Owners, permissions and symbolic links are kept, and a restore puts the folder back as it was. System folders and the panel's own folders cannot be backed up.
backups.restore_folder_body: The current content of {folder} is replaced by the backup. Files added since the backup are deleted.
backups.sftp_hint: Another server you can sign in to over SFTP (SSH), such as a storage box or a second VPS. Use an account that is only for backups. The panel tests the connection before saving.
backups.sftp_password_keep: A password is saved. Leave empty to keep it.
backups.sftp_key_hint: Paste the whole key, from -----BEGIN to END-----. Its public key must be in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the backup server.
backups.sftp_key_keep: A key is saved ({key}). Leave empty to keep it.
backups.sftp_passphrase_keep: A passphrase is saved. Leave empty to keep it.
backups.sftp_public_key: Public key, for ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the backup server
backups.sftp_folder_hint: Relative to the account's home folder, unless it starts with /. It is created if needed.
backups.sftp_host_key_none: None yet: Test and save trusts the key the server presents.
backups.sftp_trust_hint: Test and save trusts the host key the server presents now, and later connections must present exactly this key. Compare the fingerprint with the output of ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub on the backup server.
backups.sftp_saved: SFTP storage works and was saved. Trusted host key: {key}
backups.sftp_key_replaced: The server presented a new host key: {key} is trusted now instead of {old}. If you did not expect this change, check the server before you rely on these backups.
backups.sftp_remove_confirm: Remove the SFTP settings? Backups already uploaded stay on the SFTP server.

cron.title: Cron jobs
cron.name: Name
cron.run_as_hint: Run a website's tasks as its own user. Use root only for server tasks.
cron.schedule_hint: Five fields: minute hour day month weekday, such as */5 * * * * (every 5 minutes) or 0 3 * * * (every day at 03:00). Server time.
cron.command_hint: A shell command, run with /bin/sh. Its output is saved in the job's log.
cron.subtitle: Commands that run on a schedule.

services.title: Services
services.confirm_stop: Stop {name}? Websites that need it stop working until it is started again.
services.confirm_panel: Restart the panel? This page reloads in a few seconds.
services.subtitle: The programs that keep your websites running.

firewall.title: Firewall
firewall.no_ufw: ufw is not installed on this server.
firewall.inactive: The firewall is off: every port that a program opens is reachable from the internet.
firewall.enable_confirm: Turn on the firewall? SSH (port {ssh}) and the panel (port {panel}) stay open. Other ports are closed unless a rule allows them.
firewall.enable_confirm_web: Turn on the firewall? SSH (port {ssh}), the panel (port {panel}) and your websites ({web}) stay open. Other ports are closed unless a rule allows them.
firewall.limit_hint: Allowed, but an address that opens 6 connections within 30 seconds is refused for a while.
firewall.protected_hint: This rule is your last way in to SSH or the panel from your address ({ip}), so it cannot be deleted here. To replace it, add the new rule first.
firewall.added_hint: These rules take effect when you turn the firewall on. Turning it on also opens SSH, the panel and the websites to everyone. To delete a rule, turn the firewall on first: ufw numbers its rules only while it is on.
firewall.added_none: No rules yet. Add the ports that other programs on this server need before you turn the firewall on.
firewall.f2b_body: fail2ban blocks addresses that keep failing to sign in, to SSH and to this panel, for one hour.
firewall.f2b_stopped: fail2ban is installed but not running. Start it on the Services page.
firewall.no_keys: root has no SSH key. Add one under SSH keys below before you turn off password sign-in, or you may lock yourself out.
firewall.keys_hint: Whoever has the private key that matches one of these public keys can sign in as that account.
firewall.key_hint: On your computer, make a key pair with the first command, then paste the line that the second one prints. Never paste the private key (the file without .pub).
firewall.key_added: The key was added for {user}. Test it with a new connection.
firewall.key_remove_confirm: Remove the SSH key {key} from {user}? Whoever signs in with it will no longer be able to.
firewall.key_weak_hint: OpenSSH refuses DSA keys and RSA keys under 2048 bits. Add an Ed25519 key, then remove this one.
firewall.keys_not_allowed: AllowUsers, DenyUsers, AllowGroups or DenyGroups keep this account out of SSH.
firewall.keys_skipped: {file} is a symbolic link or not a regular file, so the panel neither reads nor changes it.
firewall.keys_invalid: {n} line in these files is not a key the panel can read. | {n} lines in these files are not keys the panel can read.
firewall.keys_command: SSH also asks a program for keys (AuthorizedKeysCommand). Those keys are not listed here.
firewall.logins: Can sign in over SSH now:
firewall.logins_none: With the current settings nobody can sign in over SSH. Use your provider's console, or add a key.
firewall.root_yes: With a key or a password
firewall.ssh_hint: Keep your current SSH session open and check that you can sign in again before you close it. A new port is opened in the firewall automatically.
firewall.ssh_port_confirm: Move SSH to port {port}? Connect with -p {port} from now on.
firewall.ssh_saved: SSH settings saved and SSH restarted. Test a new connection before closing your current one.
firewall.subtitle: Control which ports are open and who may sign in.
firewall.waf_detect: Detect only: log attacks, block nothing
firewall.waf_hint: Stops SQL injection, XSS, file inclusion, known scanners and other common attacks. Start with "detect only" for a few days and check the events below for false alarms. WordPress and Drupal sites get the rule set's exceptions for them automatically.
firewall.rate: Rate limit (requests per second per visitor, 0 = off)
firewall.rate_hint: Counts PHP and app requests only, not images, CSS or scripts. Bursts of five times the limit are allowed; above that, visitors get HTTP 429. 10 suits most sites.
firewall.blocked_hint: One address or range per line, such as 203.0.113.7 or 198.51.100.0/24. They get HTTP 403.

settings.title: Settings
settings.cert_active: Let's Encrypt certificate for {names} ({issuer}), valid until {date}. It renews automatically.
settings.cert_none: The panel uses a self-signed certificate, so browsers show a warning. Get a free certificate for a domain that points to this server.
settings.cert_needs_web: This needs the web server (it answers Let's Encrypt on port 80). Install it on the page:
settings.domain_hint: Such as panel.example.com. Its A record must point to this server, without a proxy or CDN.
settings.cert_remove_confirm: Remove the certificate? The panel goes back to its self-signed certificate.
settings.update_confirm: Install version {v}? The panel restarts; websites keep running.
settings.update_hint: Before an update is installed, the panel checks the project's Ed25519 signature on the release's checksum list, then the SHA-256 checksum of the download. You can also run "nefo update" on the server.
settings.subtitle: The panel's certificate, updates and alerts.
settings.mail_hint: Websites (contact forms, password resets, WordPress notices) send their e-mail through your mail provider. The server relays it with Postfix, listening on this server only; the provider's password stays readable by root only.
settings.mail_hint_gmail: User name: your Gmail address. Password: an app password (Google account → Security → 2-Step Verification → App passwords), not your normal password.
settings.mail_hint_outlook: User name: your Microsoft 365 address. SMTP sending must be allowed for the mailbox.
settings.mail_hint_sendgrid: User name: apikey. Password: a SendGrid API key with Mail Send permission. Send from a verified sender.
settings.mail_hint_mailgun: Use the SMTP credentials of your Mailgun domain.
settings.mail_hint_ses: Use SES SMTP credentials and the endpoint of your region. Send from a verified address or domain.
settings.mail_hint_brevo: Use your Brevo SMTP login and SMTP key.
settings.mail_hint_custom: Port 587 with STARTTLS or 465 with SSL/TLS. Port 25 is blocked by most cloud providers.
settings.mail_password_keep: Leave empty to keep the saved password
settings.mail_from_hint: Replaces the sender of every message. Needed when the provider only accepts verified addresses.
settings.mail_remove_confirm: Remove Postfix? Websites will no longer be able to send e-mail.
settings.mail_result_deferred: Not delivered yet: Postfix keeps trying. The provider answered: {detail}

software.title: Software
software.php_hint: Install several PHP versions and choose one per website in its settings. Versions other than the distribution's come from the widely used ondrej/php repository (sury.org on Debian).
software.stopped_hint: Installed, but its service is not running. Start it on the Services page.
software.used_by: used by {n} website | used by {n} websites
software.third_party_confirm: {name} comes from the ondrej/php repository, which will be added to this server. Continue?
software.redis_hint: In-memory cache. It speeds up WordPress with an object cache plugin. Limited to a share of the memory and only reachable from this server.
software.nodejs_hint: The newest LTS release from nodejs.org, checked against its published checksum. Use it for app websites.
software.docker_hint: Run applications in containers. Their ports are published on this server only; use an app website to make one public.
software.subtitle: Install only what this server needs and uninstall what it no longer uses. Each item shows roughly how much memory it takes.
software.adminer_hint: Browse and edit your MariaDB databases in the browser, like phpMyAdmin. It is reachable only through the panel, after you sign in.
software.waf_hint: ModSecurity with the OWASP Core Rule Set, free and open source. After installing, turn it on per website in Websites → Settings → Web firewall (WAF).
software.clamav_hint: Optional extra engine for malware scans. It needs about 1.4 GB of free memory while it scans, so it suits servers with 2 GB or more.
software.node_versions_hint: Install other Node.js release lines side by side and choose one per app website. The default stays the one from the Node.js card.
software.python_hint: venv and pip (without build tools), so app websites can run Python (Django, Flask, FastAPI…) in their own virtual environment.
software.php_only: the only version, so it stays
software.group_data_hint: MariaDB stores the data of WordPress and most other applications. Redis is an optional cache, and Adminer shows your databases in the browser.
software.group_runtimes_hint: Only needed for app websites written in Node.js or Python. PHP websites do not use them.
software.group_containers_hint: Docker runs the Docker apps from the App store and your own Compose projects.
software.group_security_hint: Optional protection on top of the panel's own checks.
software.web_hint: The panel runs one web server at a time and sets every website up for it. Nginx is the lightest; Apache reads the .htaccess files some PHP applications come with; OpenLiteSpeed reads their rewrite rules and has LiteSpeed Cache built in.
software.nginx_hint: Fast and light. PHP runs in PHP-FPM, and the panel writes each website's rules for you.
software.apache_hint: Reads .htaccess files, which some PHP applications expect. Uses a little more memory.
software.web_not_panel: installed, not used by the panel
software.web_switch_blocked: To uninstall {name} or switch to another web server, delete all websites first. This server has {n} website. | To uninstall {name} or switch to another web server, delete all websites first. This server has {n} websites.
software.web_switch_hint: To switch, uninstall {name} first, then install another one.
software.remove_web: {name} is removed. The panel only does this while no websites exist, because their settings are written for the installed web server. Install a web server again before you add websites.
software.mariadb_hint: The database server for WordPress and most PHP applications. Tuned to this server's memory and reachable from this server only (remote access can be opened per database).
software.remove_php: {name} and its extensions are removed, with the libraries only they needed. No website uses this version.
software.remove_mariadb: The MariaDB server and client are removed, with the panel's settings for them. The panel asked MariaDB itself: it holds no databases now. Its data directory {dir} is kept unless you tick the box below, and installing MariaDB again uses it.
software.remove_redis: Redis and its PHP extension are removed, and PHP-FPM restarts. Websites that use Redis as an object cache (for example WordPress with a Redis plugin) lose that cache and keep working without it, a little slower; turn the plugin off first. Whatever is stored in Redis is deleted.
software.remove_adminer: Adminer's files and its internal web server are removed. Your databases are not touched.
software.remove_nodejs: The default node, npm and npx are removed from /usr/local/bin, with the release they point to unless an app website chose that version. No app website uses the default. Cron jobs and background programs that call node stop working. Other Node.js versions stay.
software.remove_python: The venv and pip packages are removed. python3 itself stays, because the system needs it. No app website runs Python; the virtual environments of old apps stay in their folders.
software.remove_docker: Docker and its Compose plugin are removed. No containers, Docker apps or Compose projects are left. Images, volumes and build cache stay in {dir} unless you tick the box below, and installing Docker again finds them.
software.remove_waf: ModSecurity and the OWASP rules are removed and the web server restarts. Websites with the firewall on lose that protection. The firewall's log is kept.
software.remove_clamav: ClamAV and its virus databases are removed. Malware scans then use the panel's own checks only.
software.remove_node_line: {name} is removed from {dir}. No app website uses it.
software.delete_data_docker: Also delete all images, volumes and build cache ({dir})
software.delete_data_warn: This cannot be undone. Make sure you have a backup of anything you still need.
software.openlitespeed_hint: Reads the rewrite rules in .htaccess files and has LiteSpeed Cache built in for WordPress. Installed from LiteSpeed's own package repository.

docker.not_installed: Docker is not installed. Install it on the Software page.
docker.name: Container name
docker.port_hint: The port is published on 127.0.0.1 only. To reach it from the internet, create an app website with the same port.
docker.remove_confirm: Remove the container {name}? Its data is lost unless it is stored in a volume.
docker.subtitle: Containers, Compose projects and images on this server. Their ports are reachable from here only.
docker.terminal_hint: A shell inside the container (bash, or sh when the image has no bash). It ends when you close this window or after 30 minutes without input.
docker.prune_confirm: Remove every image that no container uses? They are downloaded again when needed.
docker.compose_intro: A project is a compose.yaml that runs several containers together. The panel checks it before every start.
docker.compose_missing: The Docker Compose plugin is not installed. The panel installs it when you start a project.
docker.compose_down_confirm: Stop and remove the containers of {name}? Its volumes and compose.yaml are kept.
docker.compose_name_hint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, up to 40 characters. Containers are named panel-<name>-<service>-1.
docker.compose_rules: Publish ports on 127.0.0.1 only, for example "127.0.0.1:8081:80": Docker's port publishing bypasses the firewall. To make a project public, create a website that forwards to its port. Also refused: privileged containers; the server's own network, PID, IPC, user or cgroup namespace (network_mode, pid, ipc, userns_mode or cgroup: host); extra capabilities (cap_add), host devices, security_opt other than no-new-privileges, and sysctls; mounts of system folders or of the Docker socket.
docker.compose_delete_text: The project's containers and networks are removed, then its folder with compose.yaml. Images are kept.
docker.compose_delete_volumes: Also delete its volumes (the data in them is lost)

webserver.nginx_hint: Fast and light. The best choice unless your websites need .htaccess files.
webserver.apache_hint: Reads .htaccess files, which many WordPress plugins and sites moved from shared hosting rely on. Uses a little more memory.
webserver.install_body: The panel will install the web server you choose and PHP {php} from your distribution's packages. If the server uses ufw, ports 80 and 443 are allowed in it, now and whenever the firewall is turned on; with firewalld, open them yourself. This takes one to three minutes. A server runs one web server: to switch later, delete its websites first.

webserver.preset_hint_apache: Ready-made rules for common applications: a front controller in the site's folder block, which the site's own .htaccess file may replace, and protective rules that .htaccess files cannot undo.
webserver.custom_hint_apache: Added at the end of the site's VirtualHost block, in Apache syntax. Apache checks them before anything changes; if it refuses, the error is shown and the site keeps working as before. For rules per folder, a .htaccess file in the site works too.
webserver.stats_no_logs_hint: The statistics come from the website's {server} access log. They appear after the first visits.
webserver.stats_source: From the {server} access logs, as of {time}. Certificate checks are not counted.
webserver.openlitespeed_hint: Reads the rewrite rules in .htaccess files and has LiteSpeed Cache built in, which the LiteSpeed Cache plugin for WordPress uses. Also answers HTTP/3.
webserver.preset_hint_ols: Ready-made rules for common applications: a front controller that follows the site's own .htaccess rules, and protective rules that .htaccess files cannot undo.
webserver.custom_hint_ols: Added at the end of the site's virtualHost block, in OpenLiteSpeed syntax (a context block, for example). OpenLiteSpeed checks them before anything changes; if it refuses, the error is shown and the site keeps working as before. Rewrite rules can also go in a .htaccess file in the site: the panel applies its changes within seconds.
